sources.entry: lmux - Lightweight terminal built on libghostty for running Claude Code and Codex sessions, with agent status in the sidebar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/sooftware/lmux) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: lmux is a lightweight native macOS terminal app, built on libghostty, for running several Claude Code and Codex agent sessions with status shown in the sidebar.
summary.what_it_does: lmux is a native macOS terminal app built on libghostty, aimed at people who run Claude Code and Codex sessions all day. It provides workspaces, splits, and tabs in each pane. Agent state (running, needs you, done, failed) is read from Claude Code's hooks and from Codex itself, and shown as a ring on the pane and a badge on the sidebar row, with one notification per event and a shortcut to jump to the agent waiting for you. Workspaces, splits and Claude Code or Codex sessions are restored after a quit or reboot, and a History search can reopen past sessions. Claude Code prompts can be copied, rewound, or edited and resent through hover actions. The README also covers importing a cmux setup, 26 themes, and copy-as-markdown. It states that it makes no network calls.
use_cases: run several Claude Code or Codex sessions side by side
see which AI coding agent is waiting for input
resume agent sessions after restarting the terminal
search and reopen past agent sessions
undo or edit a prompt sent to the wrong pane
Korean, Japanese or Chinese text input in a terminal
how_to_run: Or download the .dmg from GitHub Releases and drag lmux.app to Applications
Launch lmux, accept the offer to install Claude Code hooks (and Codex hooks if the Codex CLI is installed)
Run claude or codex in any pane
notable: Native Swift on libghostty, about 25 MB app with no Electron or browser engine, and roughly ten settings
Agent status comes from Claude Code hooks and Codex itself, not by wrapping the claude or codex commands
Sessions and workspaces resume after quit, update or reboot; History (shift-cmd-H) finds past sessions
Can rewind a Claude Code turn or hand a prompt back for editing (Claude Code only)
Can import an existing cmux setup, including theme, fonts, shortcuts and open workspaces
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon
No Linux or Windows support; the README says a port would be a different app
Edit, remove and undo-send actions work with Claude Code only
Codex hooks must be trusted once inside Codex before status reporting works; without that it runs without them
Few configuration knobs compared with cmux; no in-app browser, SSH workspaces or PR widgets
